On Aug. 2, 2025, the Texas A&M University Police Department (UPD) received a report of a stolen electric scooter. On Aug. 23, 2025, the Texas A&M University Police Department (UPD) stopped a subject on an electric bike who was known to have a Criminal Trespass Warning for TAMU property. The subject was arrested for outstanding local warrants and Criminal Trespass. A search of the subject revealed drug paraphernalia and criminal instruments believed to be used to defeat locks. The electric bike was believed to have been stolen and seized by the police. On Aug. 24, 2025, the owner of the electric bike reported it stolen to Texas A&M Police. On Aug. 27, 2025, Texas A&M Police observed the subject again on campus near Hensel Drive riding an electric bike. He was stopped, and the investigation revealed the bike was stolen. He was arrested for Theft, Unlawful Use of a Criminal Instrument, Possession of Drug Paraphernalia, and Disregard of a Stop Sign. The suspect’s name is Jesse Broadway. Broadway is described as a white male, 33 years old, 5’11” tall, 215 lbs., with brown hair and hazel eyes. Broadway has no affiliation with Texas A&M and has an active Criminal Trespass Warning for TAMU property. His photo can be found on the Texas A&M University Police Department’s Facebook and X page. On Sept. 5, 2025, the Texas A&M University Police Department (UPD) received a report of a stolen side-by-side. The victim last observed their side-by-side at the Physical Plant Grounds Maintenance Facility at 3 p.m. on Aug. 28, 2025. The victim discovered the side-by-side missing at 2 p.m. on Aug. 29, 2025. The key was not in the ignition when it was taken. The victim’s side-by-side is described as a green 2023 Kawasaki Mule.

On Oct. 1, 2025, the Texas A&M University Police Department (UPD) received a report of a stolen electric scooter. The victim reported that they secured their scooter with a cable-style lock to a bicycle rack near the north side of Hart Hall at approximately 11 p.m. on Sept. 29, 2025. The victim returned to the bicycle rack on Oct. 1, 2025, at 8:45 a.m. and discovered that the scooter was gone. The victim located the cable-style lock cut and lying on the ground where the scooter had been secured. The victim’s scooter is described as a black, Segway Ninebot E2 electric scooter.

On Oct. 11, 2025, the Texas A&M University Police Department (UPD) recovered two vehicles prior to them being reported stolen. Patrol officers located a University owned Golf Cart at approximately 11 p.m. on the sidewalk along University Drive near Northside Garage. After identifying the victim, they advised that the vehicle was last parked at the Coke Building at 5 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 10, 2025. There was notable damage to the ignition area allowing it to be started. The victim’s vehicle is described as a silver/ grey EZGO Elite Golf Cart with maroon Texas A&M College of Architecture markings. Patrol officers located a second University owned Golf Cart at approximately 11:45 p.m. outside of the covered small vehicle parking area near the Jack K. Williams Administration Building. After identifying that the victim was the same, they advised that the vehicle was also last parked at the Coke Building at 5 p.m. on Friday Oct. 10, 2025. There was no noticeable damage to the vehicle. The victim’s second vehicle is described as a maroon IR Club Car Golf Cart with white Texas A&M lettering.

On Nov. 4, 2025, the University Police Department was contacted by a staff member who had seen the recent crime alert. They provided information that led to UPD successfully locating and recovering the golf cart on PA 20. The golf cart will be returned to the victim. This case remains under investigation. Campus crime alerts and timely warnings to the community comply with the federal Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act (Clery Act).
